items.title: Unsloth Dynamic GGUFs run Recursive's Flint MoE locally in 24GB of RAM
items.summary: Unsloth published Dynamic GGUF quants of Flint (39.8B total, 2.5B active, Apache 2.0) so it runs locally on machines with about 24GB of RAM; Unsloth reports about 125 tokens per second on a Mac and 150 on an RTX Spark, with tool calling working in Unsloth Desktop.

doubt.pushback: Repliers note the 24GB figure assumes a 4-bit quant with short context, that speed reportedly drops past about 8K tokens, and that the Q3 quant shows high KL divergence.

reception.summary: Mostly welcoming, with users starting local tests, but several caveats on the 24GB headline (4-bit, short context, Mac GPU memory limits) and one saying it still trails Qwen.

items.title: Hermes Agent gets an official Meshy plugin for text- and photo-to-3D models
items.summary: Hermes Agent can now generate 3D models through Meshy's MCP server, for example a low-poly game asset for Godot or a printable model from a photo; Hermes Desktop renders and animates rigged models inline and keeps a gallery of models and prompts.

reception.summary: Repliers liked photo-to-printable and inline rigged previews; the only cautions were that printable meshes still need tolerance checks and that topology and poly count may need cleanup before Godot.

items.title: SGLang v0.5.22: 10x faster weight loading, 2.3x DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash throughput on Hopper
items.summary: SGLang v0.5.22 adds InstantTensor weight loading (up to 10x faster), up to 2.3x output throughput for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on Hopper, 2.1x faster GLM-5.3 decode with context parallelism and MTP, up to 27% more throughput for PD disaggregation on agentic tasks, a PyTorch MPS backend on Apple Silicon, and GGUF and LoRA support in SGLang Diffusion.

items.title: Amp agent can now hand you an interactive mini-app inside the thread
items.summary: The Amp coding agent can now generate a small interactive app in the conversation to collect input or let you try options, instead of relying on typed replies.

items.title: NVIDIA puts 2,000+ simulation-ready 3D assets on Hugging Face (SimReady Central Library)
items.summary: NVIDIA's SimReady Central Library publishes more than 2,000 open simulation-ready 3D assets on the Hugging Face Hub for robotics simulation and digital twins.

items.title: Librarian Agents: agents curate their own long-context workspace, 30%+ gains out of domain
items.summary: Librarian Agents has an agent reorganize a large body of unstructured context ahead of time for downstream use instead of relying only on agentic search; the authors report 30%+ gains, including on out-of-domain tasks, and release paper and code.

items.title: Letta's FrontierMemory benchmark scores agent memory by downstream task gains
items.summary: FrontierMemory has a model or harness turn 674 past agent trajectories into memory, then measures how much that memory helps a fixed agent on 15 coding and knowledge-work tasks; Opus 5.5 and GLM-5.3 tie at 73.3%, and Letta Dream leads the harness table.

items.title: Artificial Analysis compares 14 models on MLCR-AA and HealthBench Professional
items.summary: Across two medical benchmarks, Anthropic models give the most complete answers and top HealthBench Professional raw scores, while OpenAI models are more accurate and concise; GPT-6 Astra ties Claude Sonnet 5.5 on MLCR-AA and leads the length-adjusted HealthBench score.

items.title: PrismaX open-sources pi0.5 rollout code cutting inference from 230 ms to 87 ms on a laptop GPU
items.summary: PrismaX released the rollout code from its IROS robotics demo, which runs the pi0.5 vision-language-action policy at 87 ms per inference on a laptop GPU (from 230 ms) without pruning or distillation.

items.title: turbopuffer adds NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-Embed as a native embedding model
items.summary: turbopuffer can now embed with Nemotron-3.5-Embed natively; on its enterprise PDF search benchmark the 8B model improves recall@20 by about 5% over the next best model.

items.title: Chat-only tokenizer probe ties Arena's anonymous Kibitz model to Kimi's tokenizer
items.summary: A probe using 11 Moonshot-only test tokens reads a model's tokenizer through a chat box alone: Kibitz garbled them like every Kimi model tested, while models from 7 other labs copied them exactly.

doubt.pushback: No method write-up or code to check, and the guess that Kibitz is Kimi K3.1 is unconfirmed (based on a closed SGLang PR).
